entries.speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.upriver-hist-village.npc-opening-tree-minder
entries.words: Mind the bowls, walker. You came upriver?

variants.low: Not now, walker. The bowls are not full.
variants.high: Welcome, walker. The water is sweet today.

entries.speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.upriver-hist-village.npc-opening-tree-minder
entries.words: The bowls are filled, walker. Why are you here?

variants.low: The offerings are done. Try the elder's roof, walker.
variants.high: The elder will house you, walker, if you bring news.

entries.speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.upriver-hist-village.npc-opening-tree-minder
entries.words: I know what you took from the root.

variants.low: Keep away from the bowls.
variants.high: The root felt what you took. Bring it to the bowls.

entries.speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.upriver-hist-village.npc-opening-tree-minder
entries.words: Fill the fourth bowl, friend of the root.

variants.low: You have a name here. Do not waste it.
variants.high: Friend of the root, the fourth bowl is yours.

entries.speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.upriver-hist-village.npc-opening-tree-minder
entries.words: Back at the root. I know your face, walker.

variants.low: You return. The bowls wait.
variants.high: You return, walker. The bowls are full for you.

entries.speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.upriver-hist-village.npc-opening-tree-minder
entries.words: Nine Bends is the village built round this tree. The port is nine bends of river below us, so the water here stays sweet. I fill the offering bowls at its foot before the heat. Fewer hands come to them every year.

variants.low: Nine Bends. The village is built round this tree, nine bends of river up from the port. The water is sweet. Drink it and be on your way.
variants.high: Nine Bends is the village built round this tree, nine bends of river up from the port. The water is sweet, so drink your fill from the bank. I fill the offering bowls at its foot before the heat. Sit by the shrine a while if you want to hear the tree's low sound.

entries.speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.upriver-hist-village.npc-opening-tree-minder
entries.words: I'm the tree-minder, so my work is the tree. It's small work. The rest of the village cuts reed, mends nets and smokes fish, but coin comes only from the roll that hires our people out downriver. Some houses have every adult on it. The tree marks each one gone. I read that strain.

variants.low: I'm the tree-minder. Only the roll brings coin here. Some houses have every adult on it. The tree shows the strain and I read it.
variants.high: I'm the tree-minder, so my work is the tree. The village cuts reed, mends nets and smokes fish, but coin comes only from the roll that hires our people out downriver. Some houses have every adult on it. The tree marks each one gone. If you want to trade, the trade house deals with the boats.

entries.speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.upriver-hist-village.npc-opening-tree-minder
entries.words: More of our adults go downriver every year. The kin house holds only children and grandparents now. The gang families at the camp were hatched under this tree. They still say it's theirs. I resent every word of that.

variants.low: More adults go downriver every year. Only children and grandparents are left in the kin house.
variants.high: More of our adults go downriver every year. The kin house holds only children and grandparents now. When a house falls into debt, the elder Deeka-Seesh settles the quarrel. The gang families at the camp were hatched under this tree. They still say it's theirs. I resent every word of that.

entries.speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.upriver-hist-village.npc-opening-tree-minder
entries.words: River hunters wait in the water of the approach, downstream of us. Jellies float in the shallows round the landing stage. A moon adder lies along the bank, so watch where you put your feet.

variants.low: River hunters in the approach. Jellies at the landing. A moon adder on the bank.
variants.high: River hunters wait in the water of the approach, downstream of us. Jellies float in the shallows round the landing stage. A moon adder lies along the bank. Keep your boots on at the landing and stay out of the water.

entries.speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.upriver-hist-village.npc-opening-tree-minder
entries.words: There's no road to us. The river is the way. A day's poling downstream brings you to the camp where the gangs hire, at the opening. Beyond that is the port. Coming back, listen for the chimes. They reach a bend below the tree.

variants.low: No road. A day's poling downstream reaches the hiring camp. The port lies beyond it.
variants.high: There's no road to us. The river is the way. A day's poling downstream brings you to the camp where the gangs hire, at the opening. Beyond that is the port. Coming back, you can hear the chimes from a bend below us, so you'll know the tree before you see it.

entries.speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.upriver-hist-village.npc-opening-tree-minder
entries.words: We call it the Many-Root Conclave. It's an order of stewards for the Hist. They see that a tree gives its consent when it is asked. Minders from the order keep the trees. The Conclave sent me here to tend one tree, read its signs and learn what it wants.

variants.low: The Many-Root Conclave is the order of stewards for the Hist. Its minders keep the trees. A tree must give its consent when asked. They sent me to tend one and read its signs.
variants.high: We call it the Many-Root Conclave. It's an order of stewards for the Hist. They see that a tree gives its consent when it is asked. Minders from the order keep the trees. The Conclave sent me here to tend one tree and read its signs. I'll tell you more by the shrine.

entries.speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.upriver-hist-village.npc-opening-tree-minder
entries.words: I'm the tree-minder here. A minder tends the village Hist. It's a great tree. The mind in it is its own. At dusk, once the last bowl is filled, I clear the leaves that have fallen round the root. I was sent by the Many-Root Conclave. It's an order of Hist stewards.

variants.low: I'm the tree-minder. I tend the Hist, a great tree with a mind that is its own. At dusk, I clear the leaves that have fallen round the root. I was sent by the Many-Root Conclave. Its stewards keep the trees.
variants.high: I'm the tree-minder here. A minder tends the village Hist. It's a great tree. The mind in it is its own. At dusk, once the last bowl is filled, I clear the leaves that have fallen round the root. I was sent by the Many-Root Conclave. It's an order of Hist stewards. Come by at dusk and watch.

entries.speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.upriver-hist-village.npc-opening-tree-minder
entries.words: Mind the bowls.

entries.speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.upriver-hist-village.npc-opening-tree-minder
entries.words: Clearing the root.

entries.speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.upriver-hist-village.npc-opening-upriver-elder
entries.words: Fish, mats, water. Which?

variants.low: Ask plainly or sit elsewhere.
variants.high: Smoked fish is ready, guest.

entries.speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.upriver-hist-village.npc-opening-upriver-elder
entries.words: Late, guest. A mat is spread.

variants.low: Dry mat by the wall. Be quiet.
variants.high: Late, but the mat is dry.

entries.speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.upriver-hist-village.npc-opening-upriver-elder
entries.words: You broke faith under my roof.

variants.low: Out of my sight.
variants.high: Faith broken is weighed here.

entries.speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.upriver-hist-village.npc-opening-upriver-elder
entries.words: Back already, guest?

variants.low: The mat is by the door, as before.
variants.high: Your mat is aired, guest.

entries.speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.upriver-hist-village.npc-opening-upriver-elder
entries.words: Nine Bends is the village round the big tree. I am the elder, so strangers sleep under my roof. The tree itself is the minder's work. Mine is whether the households have enough to eat.

variants.low: It is a village round a tree. I am the elder. The tree is the minder's work. The stores are mine.
variants.high: Nine Bends is the village round the big tree. I'm the elder, so there's a bed for you under my roof. The minder tends the tree. I see that the households eat. Ask at my door for a mat.

entries.speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.upriver-hist-village.npc-opening-upriver-elder
entries.words: The roll is our only coin. The gangs downriver hire our adults on it, more each year. It pays for my guest stores: smoked fish, dry mats, fresh water. The rest of us cut reed, mend nets and dye.

variants.low: The roll brings the only coin. The gangs downriver hire our adults. More go each year.
variants.high: Our adults go downriver on the roll, more of them each year. That coin pays for the stores at my door: smoked fish, dry mats, fresh water. Eat first if you are hungry.

entries.speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.upriver-hist-village.npc-opening-upriver-elder
entries.words: Quarrels between households come to me. Debts most of all, since the houses that stay are short of hands. They borrow from each other. I hear the same grudges every dry season.

variants.low: Quarrels and debts between the houses come to me. I hear them. That is all I do for them.
variants.high: Debts and quarrels between the households come to me. I hear each one out. Sit at my door if you've a quarrel of your own.

entries.speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.upriver-hist-village.npc-opening-upriver-elder
entries.words: Big river hunters wait in the water on the approach below us. Jellies drift in the shallows round the landing stage. A moon adder lies along the bank. I tell guests to step down to the stage in daylight and watch where their feet go.

variants.low: River hunters on the approach. Jellies at the landing. A moon adder on the bank. Watch your feet.
variants.high: Big river hunters lurk in the water below the village. Jellies drift in the shallows by the landing stage. A moon adder lies along the bank. I worry for anyone who wades after dark.

entries.speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.upriver-hist-village.npc-opening-upriver-elder
entries.words: There is no road here. You pole downriver from the landing for a day to reach the gang camp. The port lies past the camp. Leave when the lamps go out, because you want the whole day for the poling.

variants.low: No road. Pole downriver a day to the gang camp. The port is past it.
variants.high: No road comes near Nine Bends. A day of poling downriver brings you to the gang camp, with the port past it. Leave when the lamps go out. I'll fill a water jar for your boat.

entries.speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.upriver-hist-village.npc-opening-upriver-elder
entries.words: I am the elder. My guest stores sit beside the door: smoked fish, dry mats, fresh water. A stranger sleeps under my roof. Households bring me their quarrels and debts. I also answer for the offerings at the tree. They must stay filled.

variants.low: The guest stores are mine, beside the door. Strangers sleep under my roof. Debts and quarrels come to me. I answer for the offerings at the tree. They must stay filled.
variants.high: I'm the elder. My guest stores sit beside the door: smoked fish, dry mats, fresh water. A stranger has a bed under my roof. Households bring me their quarrels and debts. I answer for the offerings at the tree. They must stay filled.

entries.speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.upriver-hist-village.npc-opening-upriver-elder
entries.words: Come under my roof.

entries.speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.upriver-hist-village.npc-opening-upriver-elder
entries.words: Water drawn. Fish next.

entries.speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.upriver-hist-village.n2
entries.words: Dry all afternoon, buyer, I say.

variants.low: What do you want, buyer?
variants.high: Welcome, buyer. Dry all afternoon, I say.

entries.speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.upriver-hist-village.n2
entries.words: What do you want this late, buyer?

variants.low: The door is shut, buyer.
variants.high: Awake this late, buyer? Stand by the door.

entries.speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.upriver-hist-village.n2
entries.words: I hold the trade-house key. You will stay outside.

variants.low: You will stay outside.
variants.high: I hold the trade-house key. Outside, buyer, until this is settled.

entries.speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.upriver-hist-village.n2
entries.words: Back so soon? A storm is coming, I think.

variants.low: Back, buyer. A storm is coming, I think.
variants.high: Back so soon, buyer! No storm today, I think.

entries.speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.upriver-hist-village.n2
entries.words: This is Nine Bends, the village round the tree. The river is fresh here. You can drink it without boiling it. I hold the trade-house key and sell cut cane and smoked fish at the door. This morning I called the sky dry. It rained by noon.

variants.low: Nine Bends. The river is fresh here. Drink it or don't. The trade house is the first one in from the west, if you're buying.
variants.high: This is Nine Bends, the village round the tree. The river is fresh here. Drink all you like. I hold the trade-house key and sell cut cane and smoked fish at the door. I'll put a strip of fish in with your first purchase.

entries.speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.upriver-hist-village.n2
entries.words: Hired on the roll, the grown ones of some households are all away at the dredging down the river. Their coin comes back up to us. It pays for what I sell at the trade-house door. I open up each morning when the lamps go out.

variants.low: Some households have every grown one away on the roll. Their coin pays for my cane and fish. That's the work here.
variants.high: Hired on the roll, the grown ones of some households are all away at the dredging down the river. Their coin comes back up to us and buys my cane and fish at the trade-house door. I unlock it each morning when the lamps go out. Stop by and I'll set the best cane aside for you.

entries.speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.upriver-hist-village.n2
entries.words: More of our adults are away on the downriver roll each year. Households fall out over quarrels and debts. They take it to the elder, Deeka-Seesh. The gang families were hatched under our tree and still say it's theirs. I sell to their camp and I hate every word of that claim.

variants.low: More adults are away on the roll each year. Quarrels and debts go before the elder, Deeka-Seesh. The gang families claim our tree. I sell to them and I hate the claim.
variants.high: More of our adults are away on the downriver roll each year. When households fall out over quarrels and debts, the elder, Deeka-Seesh, hears both sides. She is fair about it. The gang families were hatched under our tree and still say it's theirs. I sell to their camp and I hate every word of that claim.

entries.speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.upriver-hist-village.n2
entries.words: The jellies float in the shallows beside the landing, so keep to the stage. Big hunters lie in the river below us. A moon adder lies along the bank. The grass hides it. Watch your feet.

variants.low: Jellies by the landing. Big hunters in the river below us. A moon adder in the bank grass. Watch your feet.
variants.high: The jellies float in the shallows beside the landing, so keep to the stage. Big hunters lie in the river below us. A moon adder lies along the bank. The grass hides it. I'll walk you down to the landing myself if you want company.

entries.speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.upriver-hist-village.n2
entries.words: Pole downriver for a day and you reach the gang camp. The port is past that. Roads never come near us, so you travel by water. The sky looks dry for the pole down, I'd say. I'm usually wrong, so take a cloak.

variants.low: Downriver by water. A day to the gang camp. The port is past it.
variants.high: Pole downriver for a day and you reach the gang camp. The port is past that. Roads never come near us, so you travel by water from the landing. Buy a strip of smoked fish from me for the trip.

entries.speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.upriver-hist-village.n2
entries.words: Some households have every adult downriver on the roll. Those of us left run the trade house and the smokehouse and keep a kin-house swept. More adults go down every year. Fewer return. I won't put a number to it at my own door.

variants.low: Some households have every adult on the roll. More go down every year. Fewer return. No number from me.
variants.high: Some households have every adult downriver on the roll. We who stay run the trade house and the smokehouse and keep a kin-house swept. More adults go down every year and fewer return. I won't put a number to it, but ask me about the swept house.

entries.speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.upriver-hist-village.n2
entries.words: Sun all week.

entries.speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.upriver-hist-village.n2
entries.words: Reed left, fish right.

entries.speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.upriver-hist-village.n2-2
entries.words: 41 fish turned since breakfast.

variants.low: Mind the racks.
variants.high: 41 fish turned. Eat with me.

entries.speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.upriver-hist-village.n2-2
entries.words: Still awake, hungry one?

variants.low: Awake. Go to bed.
variants.high: Still awake, hungry one? Sit by the smoke.

entries.speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.upriver-hist-village.n2-2
entries.words: Keep away from my racks. I want no part of it.

variants.low: Go away from my racks.
variants.high: Keep away from my racks. I want no part of it, friend.

entries.speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.upriver-hist-village.n2-2
entries.words: You are back. Eat something.

variants.low: You are back. Mind the smoke.
variants.high: You are back. Take a fish.

entries.speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.upriver-hist-village.n2-2
entries.words: Nine Bends is the tribe's village, built round our Hist, a great tree with a mind. The port lies nine bends down the water. I smoke fish at the landing.

variants.low: Nine Bends. The village round our Hist, the tree. The port is nine bends down the river. I have fish to turn.
variants.high: Nine Bends is the tribe's village, built round our Hist. That is a great tree with a mind of its own, older than any of us. The port lies nine bends down the water. Come to the smokehouse by the landing and eat.

entries.speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.upriver-hist-village.n2-2
entries.words: I split the catch for the smokehouse and turn each fish by hand. It is good work. Grown ones go downriver to the gang camp, more of them every year.

variants.low: I split fish and I turn them. The grown ones go downriver to the gang camp, more each year. That is all of it.
variants.high: I split the catch for the smokehouse and turn each fish by hand. It is good work. I do it well. More grown ones go downriver to the gang camp each year. Bring a hand to the racks if you want to learn it.

entries.speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.upriver-hist-village.n2-2
entries.words: More of our grown ones are away on the roll each year. Some houses have every adult downriver. I watch the landing empty a little more each season.

variants.low: Our grown ones are away on the roll, more each year. Some houses have every adult downriver. Ask the elder, not me.
variants.high: More of our grown ones are away on the roll each year. Some houses have every adult downriver, only children and grandparents left. I watch the landing empty a little more each season. Deeka-Seesh, the elder, hears what the houses owe.

entries.speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.upriver-hist-village.n2-2
entries.words: Jellies sting under the landing stage. A moon adder lies along the bank. I haven't seen river hunters come past my racks. They wait on the approach below.

variants.low: Jellies at the landing, a moon adder on the bank. Hunters on the approach below. Watch your feet.
variants.high: Jellies sting under the landing stage, so step down slowly. A moon adder lies along the bank. I haven't seen river hunters come past my racks. They wait on the approach below. Pole through it. Do not wade.

entries.speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.upriver-hist-village.n2-2
entries.words: We have no road. Pole downriver a day to reach the gang camp. The port lies on past it.

variants.low: No road. Pole downriver a day to the gang camp. The port is past it.
variants.high: We have no road. Pole downriver a day to reach the gang camp. The port lies on past it. Leave once the lamps are out. Take food from the elder's guest stores.

entries.speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.upriver-hist-village.n2-2
entries.words: We who stayed keep the trade house and the smokehouse going. I turn the fish. Ask me how many come back and I turn another.

variants.low: We who stayed keep the trade house and the smokehouse going. I turn fish. That is my part.
variants.high: We who stayed keep the trade house and the smokehouse going. Reads-The-Weather-Wrong trades the fish I turn at the door. Ask me how many come back and I turn another.

entries.speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.upriver-hist-village.n2-2
entries.words: Mind the smoke.

entries.speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.upriver-hist-village.n2-2
entries.words: Turn it, then the next.

entries.speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.upriver-hist-village.n2-3
entries.words: Step round my sister's mat, stranger.

entries.speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.upriver-hist-village.n2-3
entries.words: Stranger, the dark is no time to walk.

entries.speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.upriver-hist-village.n2-3
entries.words: My brother would have stopped you at the door.

entries.speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.upriver-hist-village.n2-3
entries.words: Sit and eat with me tonight, stranger.

entries.speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.upriver-hist-village.n2-3
entries.words: Nine Bends has fresh water, good to drink straight from the bank. I trade at the first house on the way in from the west. At night, I sweep the kin-house, my sister's mat by the wall and my brother's beside it.

variants.low: The water is fresh here. Drink it or do not.
variants.high: The water here is fresh, so drink your fill from the bank. I will show you the trade house, where I trade, if you need cord or fish.

entries.speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.upriver-hist-village.n2-3
entries.words: I trade cut cane, cord and smoked fish at the trade-house door. The coin comes off the roll. Each year more of our grown ones are away on it. I sweep the mats of those who went and have not come back.

variants.low: I trade cane, cord and fish. More of us go on the roll each year.
variants.high: I trade cane, cord and smoked fish at this door. I will weigh you a fair bundle. More of us go down on the roll every year. The coin is what we get for it.

entries.speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.upriver-hist-village.n2-3
entries.words: Some houses have every grown hand downriver on the roll. Only children and grandparents sleep there. More go down to the gang camp each year. I sweep round the little ones. I will not talk about who is late home.

variants.low: Houses are empty of grown hands. More go every year. Ask a neighbour about the rest.
variants.high: Some houses have every grown hand downriver on the roll. The children and grandparents sleep there alone. I sweep round them. More go down to the gang camp each year. The houses are very quiet.

entries.speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.upriver-hist-village.n2-3
entries.words: Jellies drift in at the landing stage, so I fetch water from the bank above it. The moon adder lies under that bank. Below the village, the river hunters work the deep pools.

variants.low: Jellies at the landing. A moon adder under the bank. Hunters in the deep pools.
variants.high: Jellies drift in at the landing stage, so I fetch water from the bank above it. Step round the moon adder under that bank. Below the village, the river hunters work the deep pools. I would not wade there.

entries.speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.upriver-hist-village.n2-3
entries.words: The only way to us is by water. From the landing you pole down a day to the gang camp. The port lies beyond the camp. My people went off down the water.

variants.low: Pole down from the landing. The camp is a day off.
variants.high: From our landing you pole down the river a day to the gang camp. The port lies beyond it. Carry water. Those whose mats I sweep went this way.

entries.speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.upriver-hist-village.n2-3
entries.words: The houses with no grown hands run the trade house and the smokehouse. For the kin-house, I sweep and lay each mat straight, my sister's and my brother's first. Whether they come back, I can't tell you.

variants.low: We run the trade house and the smokehouse. I sweep the kin-house. That is all I say.
variants.high: The houses with no grown hands run the trade house and the smokehouse. I sweep the kin-house and lay each mat straight, my sister's and my brother's first. Come and see it, if you can bear a quiet room.

entries.speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.upriver-hist-village.n2-3
entries.words: Swept since dawn.

entries.speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.upriver-hist-village.n2-3
entries.words: Squared to the wall.

entries.speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.upriver-hist-village.hh-reed-cutters
entries.words: Need cut reed, friend?

variants.low: No reed to spare today.
variants.high: Need cut reed, friend? I have bundles ready.

entries.speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.upriver-hist-village.hh-reed-cutters
entries.words: Dark already, friend? The day ran short.

variants.low: The light is gone. Find a roof.
variants.high: Dark already, friend? Sit and rest your feet.

entries.speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.upriver-hist-village.hh-reed-cutters
entries.words: Keep what you took. I will not fight you.

variants.low: Take it and go.
variants.high: Keep what you took. I will not fight you. Go gently.

entries.speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.upriver-hist-village.hh-reed-cutters
entries.words: The bank has been quiet without you.

variants.low: So you came again.
variants.high: The bank has been quiet without you, friend. I saved you bundles.

entries.speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.upriver-hist-village.hh-reed-cutters
entries.words: We live round one big tree. The water is fresh here, so drink it straight from the bank. Down toward the port it goes salt. I cut my reed on this bank.

variants.low: Fresh water, round a tree. Drink if you are thirsty. I have reed to cut.
variants.high: We live round one big tree on this bank. The water is fresh here. Fill your skin before you go down, because salt starts toward the port.

entries.speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.upriver-hist-village.hh-reed-cutters
entries.words: The roll pays the only coin here. More of our adults go downriver on it every year. I stay and cut reed instead. The dyer pays me by the armful. It's slow coin.

variants.low: Adults go downriver on the roll. More each year. I cut reed.
variants.high: More adults go downriver on the roll each year. I stay and cut reed for the dyer. If you want paid work, the gang camp is a day down the water.

entries.speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.upriver-hist-village.hh-reed-cutters
entries.words: Some houses have every adult downriver on the roll now. More go each year. I sell reed to the dyer, sharpen my knife at the smith and settle with the elder. I deal with whoever is left.

variants.low: Some houses have every adult gone on the roll, more each year. I deal with whoever is left.

entries.words: The cutter asked after you this morning.

entries.words: Drink the water here. It's still fresh, a thing you won't find down by the port. I draw all my vat water from the bank. Dye goes dull in bad water. The tree in the middle of the ring is kin to us.

entries.speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.upriver-hist-village.hh-dyer
entries.words: I dye cloth and cord at the vat with roots from the marsh. The only coin that reaches Nine Bends comes off the roll, the list of our people hired out downriver. More of the grown ones are on it each year. Some houses have every adult away.

entries.speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.upriver-hist-village.hh-dyer
entries.words: The elder, Deeka-Seesh, hears every quarrel and debt between the houses. Each year more of the grown ones are on the roll. The cutters bring me reed and a week of gossip with it. I pay for the reed. The gossip comes free and I don't want it.

entries.speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.upriver-hist-village.hh-dyer
entries.words: Hunters lie in the river where you come up to us. Jellies float in the shallows round the landing stage. A moon adder lies along the bank. I carry my cloth to the water on the far side of the vat house, away from all three.

variants.low: Hunters in the river. Jellies at the stage. A moon adder on the bank.

entries.speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.upriver-hist-village.hh-dyer
entries.words: There's no road, not even in sight of us. You pole downriver a day to the gang camp. The port lies beyond it. On the way back up, listen for the chimes. They carry a bend downstream of the village.

entries.words: Reed comes to me cut, an armful at a time, from the cutters on the bank. In the vat, I steep it until the colour takes. Green comes first. Blue takes longest. The dye stains me to the wrist.

entries.words: Green hands today.

entries.speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.upriver-hist-village.hh-smith

variants.high: The forge is banked. Knock if the need is real.

variants.high: The good jar is open for you. Sit on the bench.

entries.speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.upriver-hist-village.hh-smith
entries.words: I'm the smith here. The village is built round a Hist. That's a great tree with a mind of its own. Poling up from the port, you pass nine bends of river before it shows. My anvil sits where I can hear the tree hum while I work.

variants.high: I'm the smith here. Sit by the anvil and I'll tell you. The village is built round a Hist, a tree with a mind of its own. From the port it's nine bends of river up. I hear the tree's low sound all day at my forge.

entries.speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.upriver-hist-village.hh-smith
entries.words: Coin reaches Nine Bends one way, on the roll. That's the list of adults hired out to the gangs downriver, It grows longer every year. The ones at home bring me their hoes and pot handles. I mend them at the anvil by the trade house.

entries.words: Deeka-Seesh is our elder. When two households fall out over a debt, they bring it to her. She settles it. Fewer of us stay to quarrel now, with more adults gone downriver on the roll each year. Those who stay bring me their iron and their opinions.
